correctness.rationale: For every n>=2, contraction creates a rank-one Laplacian update. Matrix-Tree determinant lemma and P^(n-1)=J yield a finite four-overlap sum. Every bit complexity step is bounded. Independent Euler wiring exhaustive comparisons n=2..5, direct cofactor comparisons n=2..5, and sum/support checks n=2..11 all passed.

evidence: Rødland covers every fixed-k-gram shuffled ensemble and any motif; Cowan covers expected frequencies of patterns under transition-count constraints.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These stronger-domain results dominate the count identity but do not establish a polynomial-in-n bit-operation bound when the de Bruijn graph has 2^(n-1) vertices. The explicit finite-mixing evaluation is a distinct algorithmic complexity improvement.

evidence: Lin et al. establish orthogonal cycle constructions and count total tours, not order-variable exact per-motif bit complexity. Sawada and Gabrić uniformly sample full cycles. claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The prior general numerical formula implies p_n(s), but not the claimed matrix-free O(n^2) bit algorithm. Rødland Appendix B computes a generalized inverse of a 2^(n-1)-vertex Laplacian. Exploiting P^(n-1)=J to replace it with a short overlap sum is the assessed algorithmic advance.

originality.rationale: Qualified claim solely about the O(n^2)-bit explicit matrix-free algorithm, not the scalar motif probabilities: Rødland 2006 already determines the latter by general determinant and matrix-inverse methods. Relevant publications and available historical claims were compared on implication and complexity; none inspected supplied the finite-overlap specialization. Residual synonym risk remains.
residual_risks: The underlying scalar probability is a special case of Rødland (2006); only the explicit quadratic-time specialization is claimed new.
An earlier unpublished or differently named de Bruijn Green-function or string-matching computation may already provide this O(n^2) evaluation.
The order-two covariance paper uses a related rank-one technique but in different alphabet/parameter regime.

value.rationale: De Bruijn digraphs have exponentially many states in the word order. The new direct length-n calculation allows exact likelihood optimization and motif selection without constructing any of those states, a meaningful algorithmic reduction rather than a finite-table recomputation.
